name: Accuracy
description: How close your measurement is to the true/correct value

content.overview: Ever thrown darts at a bullseye? Accuracy is exactly that: how close your measurement lands to the true, correct value. Land your darts near the center and you're accurate—simple as that. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Accuracy = how close your measurement lands to the TRUE value
A thermometer reading 99.8°C for boiling water is more accurate than one reading 115°C
It's all about being correct, not about how many decimals you show
You need to already know the true value before you can judge accuracy
Don't mix it up with precision—that's a different idea (more on that next)
content.whyItMatters: Here's why this matters: in science, being accurate beats being detailed. A rough-but-right answer beats a super-precise-but-wrong one every time. If your measurement is off the mark, every conclusion you build on top of it collapses too—so nailing accuracy is step one before anything else makes sense.
